helpAddressBody.message: Type a URL, domain, or localhost address to show Go to URL first, unless a matching tab, bookmark, or history result already has that exact address. Paths, query strings, and fragments remain distinct. Enter or clicking the result navigates the source tab. Command+Enter on macOS or Alt+Enter on Windows/Linux opens and switches to a new tab in the same window. Both actions are also available in the footer and Actions menu. Bare domains use HTTPS; localhost and loopback addresses use HTTP. Pinned source tabs allow only opening a new tab. Only HTTP(S) destinations are supported. Nonempty searches also offer Search Google for “…” after local matches; with no local match it comes first. Type google React hooks or 谷歌搜索 React hooks to put Google first and search only the words after the prefix. URL navigation keeps priority for addresses. Google uses the same current-tab and new-tab actions, including pinned-tab protection. Typing stays local; only executing the Google result opens Google's search page. No online suggestions, additional permissions, or search-selection learning.

helpHint.message: Getting started, features, and common questions.

helpIntro.message: Key workflows, shortcuts, and boundaries in JustOneHop.

helpStartBody.message: Click the JustOneHop toolbar icon or press the launch shortcut to open the palette (current: $1). Change the shortcut in Settings → Keyboard, or right-click the toolbar icon to edit the binding or open this guide in a new tab.

helpSearchBody.message: The empty home shows up to 10 suggested pages and commands based on successful use in JustOneHop, with curated commands when there is little history. Recommendations keep their order until the next opening. Search tabs, bookmarks, commands, and settings in one place using English or Chinese keywords, without mode prefixes. Combine page titles, domains, tab groups, or bookmark folders in any order—for example, “new tab”, “reopen last tab”, “theme”, or “downloads”. Bookmarks and history open in the current tab with Enter or a click. Command+Enter on macOS or Alt+Enter on Windows/Linux opens a new active tab; the footer and Actions menu offer both choices. Pinned source tabs only allow a new tab. Open-tab results still switch to that tab. Browsing history from the past week joins search results. Search All History appears seventh, or at the end of shorter lists, to search all time. A slow history query does not block other results; late replies do not insert rows. Successfully opened history results share preferences with tabs at the same website address. Main search and Search All History apply habits only within the same relevance tier for the same query, show a history icon for remembered preferences. Hover or focus the icon to see why and what will be forgotten; click it to forget. You can also press Shift+Backspace on the selected result. Forgetting affects both history and tab results.

helpControlsBody.message: Right-click a result, click Actions in the footer, or press Cmd/Ctrl+K to open actions for the selected item. Lists also support Ctrl+P and Ctrl+N alongside the arrow keys.

helpBackBody.message: Press Esc, click the back arrow, or press Backspace in an empty secondary search field to go back one level with your search and selection restored. At the main search, Esc closes JustOneHop. You can also swipe horizontally in the back direction inside the panel (commonly two fingers swiping right with macOS natural scrolling). Swipe far enough for a blue arrow to appear, and a child view or menu goes back one level immediately. Inertia cannot trigger another return; wait for scrolling to settle before swiping again. The main search, a switcher launched by shortcut, and standalone Help wait for scrolling to settle before closing. Before swiping far enough, reverse direction, press a key, or click to cancel; a completed return is never undone. Horizontally scrollable text and input areas do not trigger this action.

helpTabsBody.message: Pinning, muting, and closing other tabs keep the palette open for continued cleanup. Closing the tab you opened JustOneHop from ends the palette session, including when a bulk close removes it. Bulk close preserves pinned tabs. Search a tab group’s name to manage its tabs. Choose JustOneHop: Tab Switcher to filter recent tabs inside the palette, then click a row or press Enter to switch; Cancel returns to your search. When launching the switcher with its shortcut, hold the modifier key to select and release to switch; click the search field or press Cmd/Ctrl+F to pause release-to-switch and filter by text instead.

helpTuckBody.message: “Tuck Away Tab” moves a tab into a collapsed group at the end of the window without closing or discarding it; switch to the tab from search anytime to bring it back. Enable “Auto Tuck Tabs” in Settings to automatically tuck tabs unused for 7 days. If a group needs confirmation after a browser restart, search for “recover tucked tabs”.

helpStorageBody.message: Search for “local storage”, “session storage”, or “cookies” on a webpage. Select a key on the left to preview its value on the right; Enter or Copy Value copies the original string. JSON is formatted for reading; storage is read-only. Reading cookies requests permission only for the current site’s domains, which you can revoke anytime in Chrome’s extension settings.

helpShortcutBody.message: If a shortcut is unassigned or conflicts, open Settings → Keyboard to change it in Chrome’s extension shortcuts page. Due to browser limits, Ctrl+Tab requires one-time manual setup—search for “ctrl tab” for the setup code and steps.

helpWindowBody.message: JustOneHop keeps an in-page overlay on ordinary webpages, even when the address bar has focus. If typing is unavailable, click the search field. Chrome internal pages and other pages that cannot host the overlay use a separate window.

helpPrivacyBody.message: JustOneHop has no account, server, or telemetry. Preferences and learned search ranking stay on your device; website storage values stay only in the current panel’s memory. Browsing history requires the history permission at installation. JustOneHop keeps no persistent copy of the history database; it remembers only search terms and website addresses you explicitly select and successfully open. Reading history or a failed open creates no learning record. Incognito windows do not read ordinary history or record selections.
